Choosing the best model
• Several models are built for 1 machine learning task.
– Using several subsets of the dataset
– Using several sets of features
– Using several algorithms
• Several parameters
• Which one should be used for predictions?
 Estimate the Accuracy of the model
– The known label of the test sample is compared with the
predicted result from the model
– Example - Accuracy rate is the percentage of test set samples
that the model correctly classifies
– Check the sign of over-fitting.

Choose a machine-learning model solely by the highest accuracy measured on the training data. A separate test set and checks for over-fitting are unnecessary because training accuracy fully establishes that the model will generalize.

Silhouette-Coefficient for object 𝑥𝑥
Silhouette-Coefficient [Kaufman & Rousseeuw 1990] measures the quality of
clustering
■ 𝑎𝑎(𝑥𝑥): distance of object 𝑥𝑥 to its cluster representative
■ 𝑏𝑏(𝑥𝑥): distance of object 𝑥𝑥 to the representative of the "second-best" cluster
■ Silhouette 𝑠𝑠(𝑥𝑥) of 𝑥𝑥
𝑠𝑠 𝑥𝑥 = 𝑏𝑏 𝑥𝑥 − 𝑎𝑎(𝑥𝑥)
max{𝑎𝑎 𝑥𝑥 , 𝑏𝑏(𝑥𝑥)}

Measuring Clustering Quality
• Two methods: extrinsic vs. intrinsic
• Extrinsic: the ground truth is available only for testing
– Compare a clustering solution against the ground truth using
certain clustering quality measures
– Ex. Purity, entropy, precision and recall metrics
• Intrinsic: the ground truth is unavailable
– Evaluate the goodness of a clustering solution by considering how
well the clusters are separated, and how compact the clusters are
– Ex. Silhouette coefficient
• ranges from -1 to 1, where a high value indicates that the data point
is well matched to its cluster and poorly matched to neighboring
cluster.
